start.BlackMarsh.body,Smugglers seized the Emperor's courier on the road from Helstrom and carried his satchel into a ruin in the marsh. Your sealed orders are in it.
start.Elsweyr.body,Bandits took a caravan of Dwemer brass bound for Sentinel, and the Emperor's courier who rode with it. Your sealed orders are somewhere in their hold.
start.IliacBay.body,Your ship to Daggerfall goes down in a storm, and you wake in a pirates' cave on the coast. The Emperor's sealed orders were lost in the wreck. The tide may have carried them in.
start.Imperial.body,The Blades test the Emperor's agents before they trust them. Your sealed orders lie at the heart of a disused prison near the Imperial City. Bring them out, and you have passed.
start.Imperial.where,An old prison near the Imperial City
start.Morrowind.body,Diggers near Mournhold broke through into old Dwemer halls and fled what they found. The Emperor's courier went down after them with your sealed orders. Neither came back up.
start.noSite,No way to that province could be found. Your story begins in the Iliac Bay.
start.page.hint,Click one, or up/down and Enter, or press 1 to {n}
start.page.lead,Choose where this character wakes. Wherever it is, the Emperor's orders send you to Daggerfall, and the main story begins when you get there.
start.page.shut,The land past the Bay is off
start.Skyrim.body,The Emperor's courier sheltered from a blizzard in an old hall near Solitude, where the dead do not rest. He carried your sealed orders, and he never came out. You go in after him.
start.Sumurset.body,A scholar of the Mantella was to hand you the Emperor's sealed orders. She was found dead in the hall near Alinor where she kept her notes, and the orders are still inside.
start.Valenwood.body,A wounded Blades courier crawled into a cave near Falinesti to hide from the men hunting her. She carried your sealed orders. Find her.
start.Valenwood.where,A cave under the roots near Falinesti

tutorials.chapters.body1,Online, quests raise your standing with each guild by at most {max} a real day (days start at midnight UTC). Any more is added on later days.
tutorials.chapters.body2,Reviews promote you up to rank {cap}. Ranks {officer} and {master} are chapter chairs, won by Merit at each Sunday's Turning. A notice board explains chapters.
tutorials.chapters.trigger,When you first come online as a member of a guild, temple or order.
tutorials.characterSheet.skillRaise,A used skill goes up when you rest or travel, at most once every 6 hours.
tutorials.characterSheet.skillRaiseStats,A used skill goes up when you rest or travel, at most once every 6 hours. Your Stats page shows how close each skill is.
tutorials.crafting.body,Online, stand at a station and press {Professions}: the Crafting page opens on it. Cook at any fire.
tutorials.crafting.more,Your home can hold stations too. Each crafting profession under {Professions} says more.
tutorials.crafting.shops1,Forge: Weaponsmiths, Armorers. Loom: Clothing Stores. Workbench: Furniture Stores, joineries.
tutorials.crafting.shops2,Jeweler's bench: Pawn Shops, Gem Stores. Mason's bench: General Stores. Alchemy: Alchemists, Mages Guilds. Enchanting: Mages Guild halls.
tutorials.guilds.body1,Join a guild for its services and its work. Do that work and practice the skills it teaches to rise in rank.
tutorials.guilds.body2,You may join one temple, one knightly order, and as many guilds as will have you.
tutorials.guilds.online,Online, reviews promote you no further than rank {cap}. Ranks {officer} and {master} are chapter chairs; see Guild Chapters.
tutorials.guilds.trigger,When you first visit a guild.
tutorials.kingsGambit.body1,A game of armies and kings, played on a board laid across a tavern's card table. Choose a regular to play, set down your stake and raise your army.
tutorials.kingsGambit.body2,Each turn, move your pieces, strike and drink potions. Bring down the enemy king to win, and guard your own.
tutorials.kingsGambit.trigger,When you first sit down to The King's Gambit.
tutorials.questlines.body1,The Quests tab lists what each quest asks of you and ticks off each step. Some quests make you choose, and end differently for each choice.

tutorials.questlines.gearBody,Some quests, once finished, let you pick one of three pieces of gear: the quest’s page says so. Questlines are longer stories told in several quests, one after another. The same tab lists them.
tutorials.questlines.trigger,When you first take a quest with objectives.
tutorials.skyKetch.body1,Every ten hours the Sky-Ketch stays over the fields east of the capital for seven hours. Ride its anchor-lift up with your party, eight players at most.
tutorials.skyKetch.body2,Carry aether cells to the engine. A hit makes you drop the cell. Nets catch a fall; only death wakes you in the fields below.
tutorials.skyKetch.trigger,When you first ride the anchor-lift up to the Sky-Ketch.
tutorials.wildZone.body1,Players may fight one another in Cyrodiil and on the open {word} Ocean, where monsters are tougher and spoils richer.

tutorials.wildZone.body2,If another player kills you there, nothing drops. They may take one uninsured worn piece, or else one policy's gold, or else a tenth of your coin and letters of credit. Any other death costs the usual tenth.

Every {every, plural, one {round} other {# rounds}}, warning cells turn into fire ({fire}), spikes ({spikes}) or poison ({poison}). A piece that ends its turn on one loses that much health.

cards.kingsGambit.guide.online.body,Sit at the board, build your army and press Ready. The game starts when both players are ready. Each turn lasts {s} seconds. If your clock runs out {idle, plural, one {# turn} other {# turns}} in a row, you lose.

cards.kingsGambit.guide.onlineGold.body,At the gold table both players stake the same amount: {stakes} gold. The winner takes the pot, both stakes. If you lose, forfeit, leave mid-game or let the clock run out, the other player takes it.
cards.kingsGambit.guide.regular.body,Each regular plays at a rank. A higher rank means a bigger army, more potions, fewer blunders and a higher minimum stake.

cards.kingsGambit.guide.stake.body,Stake {a}, {b} or {c} times the regular's minimum stake. If you win, you get back {pay} times your stake. If you lose, forfeit or stand up mid-game, the regular keeps it.

cards.kingsGambit.guide.strike.body,A melee piece strikes the cell next to it. A ranged piece shoots up to {range, plural, one {# cell} other {# cells}} when nothing is in the way. A hit does {low}% to {high}% of the attacker's attack.

coll.look.shadowcloak,A hooded cloak of shadow and crimson light.

coll.look.vampirichaze,A dark violet haze smouldering about you, drops of blood rising from the ground like embers and turning into Daedric runes.
coll.look.witchfire,A coven’s green fire round your feet, tallow candles burning in its ring.

account.refusal.chaptersClosed,The guilds do not keep your standing on the realm yet.

coll.tunes.how,Foes sometimes drop sheet music. Use a sheet to add its tune. Make a placed piece a Music box in your house to play them.

coll.whole.character,It shows beside the name of each member of such a guild, on that character - your account does not keep it.

credits.ambientText.terms,Used with the author’s permission, with the author’s own lines.

credits.ambientText.what,Now and then, a short line about your surroundings: 918 written by the author, chosen by the kind of place or dungeon you are in, the hour and the weather. It stays quiet indoors and waits longer after each line.
account.refusal.codesMoved,Your recovery codes changed in the meantime. Try again.
credits.basicRoads.terms,Used with the author’s permission. The road painter is under the MIT License (Copyright (C) 2020 Hazelnut).
credits.basicRoads.what,Roads and tracks across the Iliac Bay, from the author’s hand-drawn network, painted into the ground. Shown in both skins and on the map.

credits.betterAmbience.terms,Used with the author’s permission under the MIT License, with the 29 sound clips the mod uses, from the author’s repository. Its rain and snow particle changes are not included.

credits.betterAmbience.what,The camera shakes when you are hurt, more for bigger hits. Each dungeon gets its own fog color and light, and an echo on every sound. Rain can be heard, muffled, indoors and at dungeon entrances. Its own footsteps with an armor clank stay off while Immersive Footsteps is on, as that mod’s author asks.
credits.classSkins.terms,Used with the artists’ permission, on Mac’s word. The archive states no license. Its 1,683 pictures are included unchanged.

credits.classSkins.what,Daggerfall’s classes as looks for your character in third person: acrobat, assassin, burglar, bounty hunter, dark acolyte, Dark Brotherhood, healer, monk, nightblade, pirate and sorcerer, most in both sexes, plus the original adventurer, in 20 redrawn sprite sheets. Pick one on your profile’s Skin card.
account.refusal.commissionCrafter,There is no crafter by that name.

credits.climatesCalories.terms,Reworked from the mod’s rules with the author’s permission, passed on by Mac. Its numbers were the starting point, and its own art is used for spoiled food, raw meat and the waterskin.

credits.climatesCalories.what,Survival. You feel the temperature from the climate, season, hour, weather, clothes and armor. Hunger, thirst, sleep and wetness are needs, food spoils, you can make camp and light campfires, and where you sleep matters. There are four tiers in Settings: Off, Boons (the default: neglect costs nothing, and staying fed, watered and rested gives bonuses), Casual (neglect only borrows stamina, which comes back once the need is met) and Hard (needs can hurt your attributes and health and make you sick).
credits.comeSailAway.terms,Used with the author’s permission, with his own pictures and sounds. Some wave textures are rebuilt from your own Daggerfall files.

credits.comeSailAway.what,A boat of your own to sail. Buy one as parts or as a deed, put it in the water (near a port for a deed) and take the helm. Row with the oars, or raise the sails, trim them to the wind and let it carry you. Pack the boat up to carry it with you. Includes his boats, sails, oars, wind gauge, waves and sounds.
credits.contact.forumsOrNexus,{author}, through the DFU forums ({forums}) or the Nexus page ({page})
account.refusal.commissionElsewhere,That commission is filled at the boards of its own region.
credits.daggerfall.what,The original game. All of its art, sound, text and world data are read from your own copy’s ARENA2 folder. None of it is included here.

credits.dex.terms,Ported from the shipped bundle and the authors’ own source; their art carried byte for byte (Daggerfall’s own sprites among it rebuilt from your files) - see vendor/daggerfall-enemy-expansion/README.md for the permission record.

credits.dex.what,Fifty new enemies and the encounter tables they come from (DEX): goblins, trolls that get back up, minotaurs, golems, Dwarven centurions, mounted knights, necromancers, witches, the Vengeful King Lysandus and more, ported from the authors’ own source, in Kamer’s and Kab’s art - Daggerfall’s own sprites among it, some under their paint - and in Morrowind’s bodies where Morrowind has the creature.
credits.dfo.what,The engine and systems this project was forked from. Maintained for Daggerfall Forever by Alex 13 Uslavtsev.

credits.dfu.what,This game began as a rewrite of Daggerfall Unity and still uses it as its reference. Its quest scripts, book index, settings tables, game text table, interaction-mode icons and mouse cursor are included unchanged (MIT License).
credits.diverseWeapons.terms,Used with the author’s permission. The script is under the MIT License, and the sprites are the author’s own paintings.

credits.diverseWeapons.what,First-person sprites for 18 weapons in every metal, plain and enchanted, where the original game has one sprite per weapon class. Includes double-size idle sprites for Weapon Widget and matching inventory icons.

credits.dynamicSkies.what,The sky with Enhanced environments on: a sun and atmosphere (built on Feral Pug’s extension of Unity’s procedural sky), 2 cloud layers for each weather, twinkling stars, Masser and Secunda moving through their phases, its own fog colors and distances, longer sunrises and sunsets, lightning flashes in storms, and pixel snow. The shader, presets and textures are the mod’s own. The Classic skin keeps Daggerfall’s painted sky.
account.refusal.commissionNotMade,A commission must be filled with a piece you made.
credits.eyeOfTheBeholder.terms,Used with the author’s permission, with the mod’s own 3,035 sprites.

credits.eyeOfTheBeholder.what,Third person without Morrowind data. Scroll the mouse wheel to swing the camera out behind your shoulder. It moves clear of walls, and you are drawn as the mod’s own sprite from 8 directions, standing, walking, attacking and casting, on foot or riding.
credits.foraging.terms,Used with the author’s permission, with his own quests and textures, and 6 bugs fixed.

credits.foraging.what,Make a living in the wilderness. Use a Wood-Axe to chop wood, a Pick-Axe to mine gems and metals, a Sickle to cut plants, a Spade to rob graves, a Fishing-Net to fish and a Basket to forage for food. It works by daylight, away from towns and enemies, depending on your attributes, the climate and the season. You can also fetch firewood for commoners and nobles. Its quests use 4 actions from Jagget’s Quest Actions Extension, rewritten here with thanks.
credits.grimoireUi.terms,Used with the author’s permission. The pictures and fonts are the author’s own art, included unchanged.

credits.grimoireUi.what,Daggerfall’s screens redrawn at three times the detail, with parchment and wood instead of stone, a spellbook that looks like a book, and new lettering in two fonts. Choose it under Overhauls, on the UI Overhaul card.
credits.handheldTorches.terms,Used with the author’s permission, with the mod’s own textures.

credits.handheldTorches.what,Carrying a light takes a free hand. Drawing a two-handed weapon stows or drops your torch, and it lights again when your hand is free. Keys light, put out, drop and throw a torch, and a thrown torch can set an enemy alight. In first person you see your hand holding the light. Dropped torches keep burning, light the room, can be picked up and stay after a save.
credits.horseCart.terms,Used with the author’s permission, with the mod’s own horse art.

credits.horseCart.what,Your horse and wagon stay in the world. They wait where you dismount, or follow you or stay on command. Hitch the horse to the wagon, mount by walking up to them, and call them to you outdoors. Reach the wagon from an entrance it is parked near. Its load shows by weight and its wheels turn. Online, other players see them where you left them.
credits.iliacPuddle.terms,Used with the author’s permission. The coastline is rebuilt from your own Daggerfall files.

credits.iliacPuddle.what,Makes the Iliac Bay a real sea. The seafloor falls away from every coast to as deep as 250 meters, and you can see the surface from above and below. Swim in open water: dive, surface, put on a burst of speed, climb out onto the shore and watch your breath. The deep has its own fog and light, weed, coral and schools of fish, its own creatures, and wrecks and sunken treasure under their guard.
credits.immersiveFootsteps.terms,Used with the author’s permission, from the author’s MIT-licensed source, with the mod’s 210 sound clips.

credits.immersiveFootsteps.what,Footsteps that match the ground: grass, gravel, sand, mud, snow, stone paths and shallow or deep water outdoors, tile, stone or wood floors indoors, dungeon water, and leather, chain or plate boots on stone. Your armor rattles as you walk, and the mod adds its own landing and splash sounds. Comes in 2 sound qualities.
credits.kingsGambit.terms,Used with permission, on Mac’s word. The bundle names no author.

credits.kingsGambit.what,A battle of armies and kings, played at a tavern’s card table against the regulars, or online against another player. Its units use the Iliac Hand cards’ pictures, and its kings the Bay deck’s.
credits.l10n.bundled,Daggerfall’s original text is {pack}, used with its authors’ permission.
credits.l10n.checked,Machine translation by Claude, checked and corrected by {names}.
account.card.codesLeft,{n, plural, one {# left} other {# left}}
account.refusal.commissionPiece,That piece is not what the commission asks.
credits.l10n.machine,Machine translation by Claude, still being checked. Corrections from native speakers are welcome.
credits.layeredArmor.terms,Made for DFO and carried under the owner's exception for art drawn from Daggerfall's own (vendor/layered-armor/README.md).

credits.layeredArmor.what,The art of the Layered Gearing look: every helmet, chest and leg armor in leather, chain and plate of seven metals, and the cloaks and hoods, for both bodies, made for the game from Daggerfall's own class and enemy sprites.
credits.meanerMonsters.terms,Used with permission under its MIT License (Copyright (C) 2020 Ralzar; Author: Hazelnut & Ralzar).

credits.meanerMonsters.what,Twenty monsters made tougher, with new damage, health, level and armor. Rats, bats and zombies are gentler. Werewolves and wereboars are a fifth larger, and the dragonling is two and a half times its size. Based on version 1.5.2. With the combat overhaul on, Kirk.O’s version of these numbers is used instead.
credits.mudex.terms,Used with permission, on Mac’s word; its two tables carried byte for byte. The repository states no license.

credits.mudex.what,Meaner Unleveled Daggerfall Enemy Expansion: Meaner Monsters as its author made it for Daggerfall Enemy Expansion. With both on, it sets the stats of 35 monsters, old and new, and gives every kind of dungeon its own themed, unleveled encounter tables.
account.refusal.commissionRecipe,Only pieces the market lists may be commissioned. Arrows and siege works cannot.
credits.oblivionLeveling.terms,Used with the author’s permission, on Mac’s word. The archive states no license and names no author.

credits.oblivionLeveling.what,Another way to level, offered when you create a character. Raising skills fills a 100-point bar instead of Daggerfall’s skill total: primary and major skills fill it fastest, minor skills next and the rest slowest, and any overflow carries into the next level. Each level up gives you points to spend on a few attributes, with Luck costing more. You can set the points, how many attributes, and Luck’s cost on the mod’s tile. Originally an OpenMW Lua mod for Morrowind.

credits.oceanHoles.what,Blue holes in the deep. Far out in Iliac Puddle No More’s sea, the seafloor drops into a black pit under a plume of miasma. Swim down to reach a drowned, lightless dungeon where creatures of the deep replace the fire creatures, and loot is one material better.
credits.pcaao.terms,Used with the author’s permission. Based on the released mod and its public source, which states no license.

credits.pcaao.what,The combat overhaul. Armor reduces the damage you take instead of your chance to be hit, and your skills and stats decide whether you hit. Weapons and armor wear by their kind and material, using his Believable Equipment Characteristics And Durability. Shields block by their material and your stats, critical hits multiply damage, and monsters have their own hides. His versions of Ralzar’s Meaner Monsters and of Roleplay & Realism’s archery apply when those mods are on.
credits.pixelifyGlyphs.terms,The game's own work (vendor/pixelify-glyphs/, built by tools/pixelifyGlyphs.py).
credits.pixelifyGlyphs.what,Two glyphs drawn for the enhanced skin on Pixelify Sans's own grid: a 2 and a Z that can no longer be taken for each other.
credits.raidingParties.terms,Made by Kamer for this game, used with his permission, with some bugs fixed.
account.refusal.commissionsCrafterMax,That crafter already has {max} commissions waiting, the most one crafter can have.

credits.raidingParties.what,Raids on towns across Tamriel. Each day knights, bandits or orcs attack for 2 hours (10 real minutes online). Drive off 15 to 25 of them, with the town watch beside you, to free the town and raise your standing.
credits.raum.terms,The author’s own work, from his repository.

credits.raum.what,The book you read Daggerfall’s books in on the Enhanced skin: project-raum’s leather journal, with a cover that opens, two-page spreads, pages that turn, and torn, stained paper. The text is Daggerfall’s own, in its own fonts.
credits.rr.terms,Used with the author’s permission under the MIT License.

credits.rr.what,The mod’s rule changes: bows hit harder the longer you draw them, no climbing with a weapon out, swing speed from both speed and strength, smaller to-hit bonuses from materials, armor that wears from blows, the classic strength bonus, bank loans by level, ships boarded only from port towns, an encumbrance penalty, lights put out when you leave a dungeon by day, a purification potion that cures poison, varied looks for human enemies by class, expulsion from the Thieves Guild and Dark Brotherhood for poor work, hand-to-hand training at the Fighters Guild, and beds you can click to sleep in. Also its NPC variants, enhanced riding, refined training and the Master Armorer quests.
credits.rrItems.terms,Used with the authors’ permission under the MIT License. The 280 sprites are the authors’ own art.

credits.rrItems.what,Two new weapons, the Archer’s Axe and the Light Flail, and a light and a medium armor set in every metal, with their own inventory and paper-doll art. Also changes what items weigh and cost, and adds its loot tables, enemy gear, starting kits and shop stock.

credits.seasons.what,Autumn, spring and winter repaints of the trees, rocks and plants in woodland, hill, haunted and mountain areas. The textures are not included: they are read from your own copy of the mod.
credits.shieldWidget.terms,Used with the author’s permission, with the mod’s own 600 sprites.

credits.shieldWidget.what,Shows your shield in first person, which the original game never did. It is drawn in its own metal and looks more battered as its condition drops. It slides away when you sheathe, swing or cast, bobs as you walk, raises and lowers, and rocks when a blow lands on it.
credits.silkscreen.terms,SIL Open Font License 1.1. The license is included with the glyph.
credits.silkscreen.what,The digit 5 in the Enhanced skin’s numbers. Pixelify Sans’s 5 looks like an 8, so this one digit comes from Silkscreen.
credits.spellIcons.what,Additional spell icons for the spell maker and spellbook.

credits.travelOptions.terms,Code under the MIT License (Copyright (C) 2020 Hazelnut; PlayerAutoPilot Copyright (C) 2019 Jedidia). The 3 interface textures are the mod’s own art, used with the author’s permission.

credits.travelOptions.what,Travel across the land instead of arriving at once. The travel map lets you choose Daggerfall’s fast travel or a sped-up journey, with a panel to steer it, stops for encounters and places, and a key to follow Basic Roads’ roads and tracks. The travel map also gets a ports filter, a page with the road network drawn on it, a location info key and location markers. The autopilot is Jedidia’s, from Tedious Travel.
credits.unleveledLoot.terms,Used with permission under its MIT License (Copyright (C) 2020 Ralzar).

credits.unleveledLoot.what,Loot and shop stock no longer scale with your level. Weapon and armor materials depend on your luck, the shop’s quality and the kind of dungeon. Gold on bodies is divided by your level and multiplied by your luck. Daedra and Orcs can drop their own metals, and any material can stand in for another.
account.refusal.commissionsMax,You may have {max} commissions posted at once.
credits.vorbis.terms,From vgmstream’s table (ISC-style license) and libvorbis’s encoder output (BSD-3-Clause, Xiph.org). Both licenses are included with the files.
credits.vorbis.what,Two Vorbis setup headers that Unity audio clips leave out. With them, Come Sail Away’s 5 sounds play exactly as the author made them.
credits.warmAshes.terms,Used with the author’s permission. The quests are his own, unchanged, and the ships are his edits applied to your own game files.

credits.warmAshes.what,Pirate ambushes at sea. Fast travel by ship can be attacked by pirates: you fight on your ship’s deck with your crew (on a borrowed ship if you own none), with the raiders’ ships nearby. Beat them and you land where you were headed. Includes his 4 quests and 6 ship layouts.
credits.weaponSheathing.terms,The mod’s own permission: free to use with credit and no fee.

credits.weaponSheathing.what,Sheathed Morrowind weapons stay on your body, at the hip or on the back in their own scabbards, with a quiver for a bow. Its 71 scabbard models and 3 skeleton add-ons are included and work as they do in OpenMW. The scabbards are by akortunov, Greatness7, Heinrich, London Rook, Lord Berandas, Melchior Dahrk, MementoMoritius, Petethegoat, PikachunoTM and Remiros, as the mod’s readme credits them.

credits.weaponWidget.what,Reworks the first-person weapon. Swings wind up from the idle pose and recover, the weapon shows in the hand you swing with, and sheathing slides it off the screen. Adds a walking bob, look inertia, stepped movement, double-size idle sprites from the mod, and recoil when you hit, parry or miss. The Morrowind arms move the same way.
account.refusal.commissionUnyielded,Nothing produces what that piece is made of yet, so no one could make it.

credits.windmills.what,Windmills: the tower and its sails, the machinery inside with its turning gear and roller, 17 climate and season looks, and the 7 farms he chose for them. Enhanced skin only. The Classic skin shows Daggerfall’s own farms.
credits.worldOfDaggerfall.terms,Used with the author’s permission, confirmed by Mac.

credits.worldOfDaggerfall.what,The wilderness: his 65 layouts of bandit camps and forts, ruins, shrines, mountains and rock fields, listed at 227,938 places across the Iliac Bay, one to a map square, with the bandits, bears, warriors and treasure they hold. Also his camp outside Privateer’s Hold.
credits.worldTooltips.terms,Used with permission under its MIT License (Copyright (c) 2009-2018 jefetienne), with a second MIT notice for Daggerfall Workshop.

credits.worldTooltips.what,Shows a name under the crosshair for what you are looking at: a person, a shop sign and its opening hours, a door and its lock level, a dungeon entrance, a lever, a wheel, a ladder, a bookshelf, a summoned Daedra, and what a chest or a body holds. On the Enhanced skin it appears at the crosshair instead of in the mod’s tooltip panel.

effect.look.aetheric,Crystal shards rise off the ground and gather into a turning ring. It opens with a chime of its own.
effect.look.ashen,A foe you kill crumbles to ash from the feet up. Bone shards fall, and grey dust rolls out over the ground.
effect.look.automaton,Your horse wears riveted brass plates set with aetherium studs. Sparks fly off its hooves, and steam breathes from its chest.
effect.look.brass,A ring of brass cogs turns round a blue aetherium core. Steam vents at its foot.
effect.look.daedric,A jagged arch of black iron thrusts up round a crimson vortex. Its runes crawl, embers rise, and it opens in a burst.
effect.look.dawnfire,Your horse turns radiant gold, its legs burning up from the hooves. Its mane is golden fire, and its hoofprints burn.
effect.look.pyre,A Daedric sigil burns into the ground under the foe you kill. A pillar of crimson fire takes it, and embers storm upward.
effect.look.runic,Your portals turn ice-blue inside a ring of carved runes that glow as it turns.
effect.look.spectral,Your horse turns to a pale blue ghost that fades at the legs. Light wisps off it, and its hooves leave glowing prints.
effect.look.tonal,The foe you kill bursts into brass cogs and steam. A blue tonal ring rolls out over the ground.
effect.look.voidrend,A rift tears open in the foe you kill. Its shards spiral into the void, and the rift snaps shut in a ring of violet light.
effect.look.warhorse,Your horse turns black and crimson under scaled barding with burning edges. Its mane burns, and smoke and embers roll off its hooves.

features.armoryOthers.note,Whose Aura Armory pieces are shown. Near shows the players close to you. Your own pieces always show.

features.banthaJungle.note,Bantha, from Lainlyn to Mournoth, becomes dense jungle: giant trees overhead, palms, ferns and broad leaves underfoot, and a humid haze that is thickest at dawn and in rain. Off keeps its original woods.

features.beastFeet.note,With the Morrowind body, how a Khajiit's or an Argonian's boots and shoes are drawn. Shafts only keeps a boot's shaft over the bare foot and hides shoes; Hidden hides all footwear, as in Morrowind.
account.refusal.fenced,The Broker already settled that sale. Open her window again.

features.beastHelm.note,With the Morrowind body, how a Khajiit's or an Argonian's helmets are drawn. Open only hides closed helmets but keeps open ones such as the chain coif, as in Morrowind; Hidden hides them all.
features.blood.effect,Takes effect at once; the number of marks that stay changes when the game next loads or you enter a dungeon.

features.blood.note,Stains stay on floors and walls where blood lands. A big killing blow sprays it further, and a heavy hit on you splashes a few drops on the screen. The slider sets how much, from Light to Abattoir; Off keeps the classic splash that fades away.
account.refusal.firmCharacter,This character could not be found for the Firmament. Try again.
features.bowsLeftHand.effect,Takes effect on the next weapon you equip.
features.bowsLeftHand.note,Bows go in your left hand only, so you can keep a one-handed weapon in your right and switch between them. Off by default in Daggerfall Unity.
features.calmHud.note,Your health, fatigue and magicka bars fade away while all three are full, and come back the moment one changes.
features.chooseGuildJobs.effect,Takes effect the next time a guild offers you work.
features.chooseGuildJobs.note,Guilds show you a list of the jobs you can take instead of giving you one at random. Off by default in Daggerfall Unity.
features.city247.note,Keeps city gates, shops, guild halls, banks, and libraries open at all hours.
account.refusal.firmClosed,The Firmament isn't available to you right now.
features.cloudQuality.note,How detailed the clouds in the enhanced outdoors are. Low is lighter on your machine; High looks best if you have power to spare.
features.combatVoices.note,You and your enemies grunt when swinging and cry out when hit. The sounds are in the original game but go unused. On by default in Daggerfall Unity.

features.dungeonEncounters.note,Some dungeon rooms hold an encounter: a ward to hold against foes, sources or seals to break, or a puzzle to work out. Win one to open its vault. Online, your party wins it together.
features.dungeonMap3d.note,The enhanced map shows dungeons in 3D, hand-drawn: turn, tilt and zoom it, with every floor you’ve explored at its own height. Off shows one flat floor at a time.
account.refusal.firmKey,One of those stars is unknown.

features.dungeonWallStyle.note,Which textures dungeon walls use: Classic, the region’s climate (Climate) or random (Random). Climate and Random keep main-story dungeons classic; Climate Only and Random Only change them too. Classic by default in Daggerfall Unity.
features.effect.gameLoads,Takes effect when the game next loads.
features.effect.nextDungeon,Takes effect on the next dungeon you enter.
features.effect.nextMap,Takes effect the next time a map is opened.
features.effect.worldLoads,Takes effect when the world next loads.
features.enemyInfighting.note,Monsters attack anything they aren’t allied with, not just you: a bear fights a spider, a Daedra fights a knight. On by default in Daggerfall Unity.
features.enhancedAi.effect,Takes effect at once; pathfinding from the next dungeon you enter.
account.refusal.firmPath,A star has no path back to your birthsign.

features.enhancedAi.note,Enemies take turns, back off when hurt, and archers keep their distance. Big attacks are marked on the ground: hit hard to stagger them or dodge. Red, hatched attacks can’t be stopped. Trees, rocks and crates block sight and missiles. Pathfinding works in dungeons only for now; towns, interiors and doors come later. Off keeps the classic behavior.

features.enhancedClimbing.note,Press Jump at a ledge to climb onto or over it, or while moving forward to vault a low wall. Jump at a high ledge to catch it and hang: Forward climbs up, Left and Right move along it, Crouch lets go. Hold Forward against any wall to climb it. Holding on wears out your grip; your Climbing skill sets how long it lasts, how high you reach and how fast you climb. Off keeps the classic climbing.

features.enhancedCombatVisuals.note,Hidden enemies can be seen: a chameleon shimmers, a shadow is a silhouette, and an invisible enemy flashes when you hit it. The rules don’t change. Off hides them as the original does.

features.enhancedEnvironments.note,A living sky with the sun, both moons and stars, clouds that build with the weather and cast shadows, falling rain and snow, and grass that bends in the wind. Off brings back the classic painted sky and weather. The third choice uses Dynamic Skies by BadLuckBurt and carademono, included with permission; its settings open on this tile.
features.enhancedLighting.effect,Lighting takes effect when the world next loads; steady shadows and calmer eye at once.

features.enhancedLighting.note,Warmer, more natural light: lanterns and torches that glow and fade with distance, light through fog, shadows from the sun and your torch, darker corners, a glow on windows and flames, and rays of sunlight. Off is the classic flat lighting. Steady shadows stops shadows flickering, at some cost to frame rate; Calmer eye slows how fast your eyes adjust to light and dark.
features.enhancedMap.note,One hand-drawn parchment map for the world, towns and dungeons, held in your hands, that you can pan and zoom. Off uses the classic three map windows.

features.enhancedSounds.note,New sounds on the enhanced UI: wind outdoors that rises and falls with its strength and goes quiet indoors, a coin clink in the enhanced inventory, hands and boots on stone when you climb, the tools when you gather, a horse that snorts and breathes, its hooves changing with the ground, the sea under a deck with its bells and its own music at the helm, surf on the shore, the wild by region and hour, and a town's street, smithies and taverns.

features.enhancedWater.note,Seas, rivers and ponds you can see into: waves that grow with the wind, foam where they meet the shore, ripples where things move, the sky and the moon on the surface. Off brings back the classic flat water.
features.firstPersonLighting.note,What you hold in first person takes the light of where you stand: your weapon, your spellcasting hands, the torch in your off hand and the Morrowind arms.
features.grass.effect,The amount takes effect when the world next loads; the style at once.
account.card.guestNote,Adding a username keeps everything this account already has.
account.refusal.firmRate,Too many changes this hour. Try again later.

features.grass.note,How much grass grows in the enhanced outdoors. Grass is the heaviest thing outdoors, so try Half first if the game runs slow. Meadow is hand-drawn tufts, flowers and bushes; Pixel is finer, older tufts; Smooth is soft, shaded blades.
features.groundSharpness.note,How sharp the ground looks into the distance. Off is the cheapest and blurs far ground; Maximum is the sharpest. Turn it down if the outdoors run slow.
account.refusal.firmRid,That request could not be read. Try again.
features.horseCare.effect,Takes effect at once. Online, each player picks their own.

features.horseCare.note,Every horse has its own Speed, Stamina, Endurance and Strength. It walks unless you hold Run to gallop, which tires it, and feeding it builds a bond that makes it better. On Boons neglect costs nothing and it is never slower than the classic horse; on Hard a hungry horse is weaker; Off is the classic horse.
account.refusal.firmStale,Your stars changed in another session. Check them and try again.
features.killFxOthers.note,Whose kill effects and mount looks are shown. Near shows the players close to you. Your own always show.
features.kind.enhanced.blurb,This game’s own changes and additions to the original.
features.kind.mod.blurb,Mods by other authors, credited by name.
features.landViewDistance.note,How far the land around you is drawn, in map squares: up to 6 with the enhanced outdoors, and up to 4 on the classic UI or with the outdoors off.
features.livingAdventurerLoot.note,Governs equipment dropped by defeated adventurers: empty, supplies only, standard humanoid, or full equipment.
features.livingAdventurers.note,Simulates rival adventurers delving dungeons across Tamriel, advancing, and leaving fallen remains.
account.refusal.foe,A death to a foe in the open zone drops nothing now. The game may need updating.
features.livingBounties.note,Rebalances notice boards toward wilderness contracts with higher payouts that lower regional crisis tension.
features.livingCamps.note,Spawns slope-aligned roadside encampments, patrol outposts, and traveller tents along highways.
features.livingDungeonMobTraits.note,Allows regular monsters and class enemies inside dungeons to spawn with combat traits and shields, scaling with player level.
features.livingMobTraits.note,Allows regular exterior foes, camps, and wilderness encounters to spawn with combat traits and shields, scaling with player level.
features.livingNaval.note,Populates open waters with multi-ship fleet skirmishes between provincial patrols and pirate squadrons.
account.refusal.fortBuilding,That work is being raised already.
features.livingNemesis.note,Dispatches persistent challengers, bounty hunters, and grudge avengers with roleplay dialogue checks.
features.livingPolitical.note,Drives regional state transitions between peace, war, plague, and civil strife across Tamriel.
features.livingQuarantine.note,Bars city gates around the clock during severe outbreaks and establishes outside relief tents.
features.livingReputationConsequences.note,Scales dynamic regional reputation reactions across prices, taverns, courts, temples, checkpoints, and nemesis pools.
features.livingRoadAdventurers.note,Spawns non-hostile adventurers travelling highways, camping in the wilds, returning with dungeon spoils, or fighting monsters along the road.
account.refusal.fortMax,That work has reached its final stage.
features.livingTravel.note,Allows journeys and fast travel to be interrupted by roadside caravans, dilemmas, or hostile ambushes.
features.livingUrban.note,Generates contained street clashes between the city watch and insurgents during regional war and strife.
features.livingWilderness.note,Controls how often Living Tamriel replaces or supplements exterior wilderness spawns with dynamic patrols, wildlife, and encounters.
features.lootRarity.effect,Takes effect on the next drop; items you wear update within a few seconds.

features.lootRarity.note,Weapons, armor and jewelry can drop as Magic, Rare or Legendary, with extra bonuses you can read and compare. The odds depend on what you killed, where, and your luck. Rare and Legendary gear is rarer early on and becomes more common as you grow. Rare and Legendary items drop unidentified. Off is the classic loot. Online, some weapons carry a sigil that grows with your Renown.
account.refusal.fortNotHere,That work cannot be raised at this seat.
features.ltEncounterScale.note,Scales the squad sizes, packs, and skirmish armies spawned by Living Tamriel (1x Low, 2x Mid, 4x High).
features.ltLocationCooldown.note,Sets how long a town waits after a street skirmish, quarantine tent, rival ambush, or citizen plea before another can start there.
account.refusal.frozen,Your account is frozen by staff. You can still talk to staff in the Staff tab.
features.ltUrbanLoot.note,Governs whether corpses of street skirmish fighters are emptied to safeguard the gold economy, drop field supplies, or drop full gear.
features.ltWildernessLoot.note,Governs loot dropped by bandit encampments, wilderness marauders, and highway checkpoints.
features.mod.beautifulTowns.effect,Takes effect the next time you start the game; loading a save is not enough. Offline it also needs Replace Game Artwork.
account.refusal.grace,The fallen player still has a moment to settle their own death. This will be tried again shortly.
features.mod.betterAmbience.effect,Takes effect at once; a dungeon’s fog and light from the next one you enter.
features.mod.climatesCalories.effect,Takes effect at once. Online, each player picks their own.

features.mod.climatesCalories.note,Hunger, thirst, sleep and the weather come into play: eat, drink, dress for the climate and rest by a campfire or in a bed. On Boons neglect costs nothing and tending earns bonuses; on Casual unmet needs drain up to half stamina and repay; on Standard needs tick slower with mild penalties, stamina repayment and boons; on Veteran survival is stern with boons, soft rust and non-fatal cold/thirst; on Hard they cost full attributes and health and can kill; Off is the classic game.
account.refusal.guest,Insignia need a registered account. Add a username and password first.
features.mod.diverseWeapons.effect,Takes effect when a weapon is next drawn.
features.mod.eyeOfTheBeholder.effect,Takes effect at once. Scroll out to leave first person.
features.mod.foraging.effect,Takes effect at once; its quests when the game next loads.
features.mod.immersiveTravel.effect,Takes effect the next time you start the game; loading a save is not enough. Fares and rules change at the next map.
features.mod.kingsGambit.note,A game of armies and kings at a tavern's card table, against a regular or another player, for gold or for fun. Off, the tables offer only Hold'em and Iliac Hand.
features.mod.meanerMonsters.effect,Takes effect on monsters that appear after the change. With Daggerfall Enemy Expansion on, it takes effect when the game next loads.
features.mod.oblivionRemasterLeveling.effect,Takes effect on the next character you make; a character keeps the system they were created with.
features.mod.physicalItems.effect,Takes effect at once; a size change applies to items that drop after it.
features.mod.projectLegacy.effect,Takes effect at once; a family keeps the model it was founded with.
account.refusal.guildAlready,This character already belongs to a guild.
features.mod.unleveledLoot.effect,Takes effect on the next drop or shop restock.
features.mod.warmAshesShips.effect,Takes effect on your next sea voyage.
features.mod.weaponSheathing.effect,Takes effect at once with the Morrowind body.
features.mod.weaponSheathing.note,With the Morrowind body, a put-away weapon hangs in a scabbard on your hip or back, and a bow gets a quiver. Off, a put-away weapon disappears, as in Morrowind.
features.mod.windmillsKamer.note,Windmills with turning sails on seven farms, with machinery inside and a look for every climate and season. Off leaves the farms as they were.
features.moddedLighting.note,Needs the Improved Interior Lighting mod. Its warm, flickering lights replace the classic lighting, and with shadows on, lamps, people and monsters cast soft shadows too.
features.mwBillboardLook.note,With the Morrowind body, bodies and horses stand as flat upright pictures, like the classic sprites. Off, they are drawn as the camera sees them in 3D.
account.refusal.guildBattle,The guild is in a siege or a Tourney this week. It cannot be disbanded until the battle is over.

features.mwBodyMotion.note,In third person a Morrowind body walks at the pace you move, carries each weapon its own way, and swings with its whole body while its legs keep moving. Off plays Morrowind’s own animations.
features.mwInventoryBody.note,Choose how your character appears in the inventory: follow third person, always 3D with Morrowind data, or always the 2D paperdoll.
features.mwItemIcons.note,With Morrowind data, items in your inventory and quickslots are shown as rendered 3D ground meshes. Off shows classic 2D item sprites.
account.refusal.guildCharacter,The account service could not tell which character that is.

features.mwModelDetail.note,With the Morrowind body, Pixelated draws bodies, horses and your arms in large pixels like the classic sprites. Sharp draws them at your screen’s full resolution and uses more video memory.
features.mwPlayerFp.note,Choose 3D Morrowind arms and weapons or classic 2D sprites in first person. Falls back to 2D without Morrowind data.
features.mwPlayerTp.note,Choose a 3D Morrowind body or your Profile 2D look in third person. Falls back to your 2D look without Morrowind data.

features.mwShoulder.note,With a Morrowind body in third person, the camera sits behind a shoulder so your head no longer hides your aim. With a weapon or a spell out it rises over your head instead, so shots land on the crosshair.
features.navalCombat.effect,Takes effect at once; Ship handling, the next time you take the helm. Online it is always on.

features.navalCombat.note,Ship battles on Come Sail Away’s boats: look to one side and hold Attack to aim a broadside, then let go to fire. Pirates, merchants and navies sail every sea. Board a ship that surrenders. Piracy is a crime.
account.refusal.guildContractsMax,A guild may have {max} contracts posted at once.
features.nearDeathWarning.note,The screen pulses as your health gets low: slowly below 40%, fast below 20%. On by default in Daggerfall Unity.

features.npcMarks.note,With Morrowind People on, a small icon bobs over the people worth finding: a yellow mark over someone a quest needs, a coin over a merchant, and a blue gem over guild trainers, guild quest givers and the arena’s officers.
features.offlineFirmament.note,Enables the Firmament constellation passive tree and Renown progression while playing offline.
features.offlineHousing.note,Buy and sell homes at the front door across all towns and hamlets, as in online DFO. Off restores classic bank housing.
features.offlineProfessions.note,Enables gathering nodes (mining, herbs, logging, hunting, fishing) and crafting professions offline.
features.offlineRespawn.note,When you die in single-player, wake at the nearest safe place at half health. You lose a tenth of your purse, instead of ending the game.
features.offlineStarfall.note,Allows fallen stars, coven defense encounters, and Morwen's questline to occur near you in offline play.

features.questHerald.note,A notice slides in when a quest begins, when its journal gains an entry, when one of its deadlines is less than a day away, and when it ends. Off updates the journal without a notice.
features.questlines.effect,Takes effect on the next quest you take; quests you already have keep the rules they began with.

features.questlines.note,Every quest shows its objectives, some let you choose how they end, some offer a piece of gear fitted to you when done, and questlines lead to the Breaches, the Battlespire and the Abyss. Off is the classic journal and its rewards, and online it is always on.
account.refusal.guildHallHave,Your guild already has a hall. Sell it first to buy another.

features.questMarks.note,Places your quests send you to are marked on the map once your map knows them, and the quest you follow is marked on the compass. Off is the classic map and compass, which mark nothing for a quest.

features.questTracker.note,A card at the top right shows the quest you track from the journal, or else the one it last updated: its newest entry, where it points and the time left. Off keeps the classic screen, with no quest card.

features.quickLoot.note,Loot without opening a window: the mouse wheel moves through the list, Activate takes one item, and the Take everything key takes all but junk (Take gear sets which gear). Off uses the inventory window.

features.quickSlots.note,Diamond puts 4 slots in a diamond at the bottom left, on keys 1 to 4. Hotbar puts 10 above your health bars on keys 1 to 0; Diamonds makes them diamonds. Drag an item or spell onto a slot, or point at it and press the key. Off hides them, but their keys still work.

features.realForests.note,Trees grow together in forests, with open grassland between them. Dungeons, ruins, shrines and camps are often hidden in the woods, and towns and farms stand in cleared fields. Deserts are unchanged. Off spreads the trees evenly, like the original.
account.refusal.guildHallMoved,The hall changed while you were selling it. Look again.

features.renderScale.note,Draws the world at a lower resolution and scales it up to fit; menus and the HUD stay sharp. Try 75% if the outdoors run slow on a big or high-resolution screen. Retro Picture Mode replaces this while it is on.

features.resourceHighlights.note,How herbs, veins, trees and other gathering spots near you stand out. Glint makes them catch the light with sparkles; Outline rings each one in its profession’s color, plain to see day or night; Both does both.
features.smallerDungeons.effect,Takes effect on the next dungeon you enter. A save made at the other size puts you at the dungeon’s start.

features.smallerDungeons.note,Dungeons bigger than five blocks are cut down to five: a center block with four around it, the same every visit. Main-story dungeons keep full size; a quest keeps the size it was set up at. Online every dungeon has its own size instead.

features.tamrielLand.note,The world goes on past the Iliac Bay over all of Tamriel. Each province has its own land, sky and trees, and its own cities, towns, roads and dungeons. Off ends the world at the Bay’s edge.

features.tamrielLands.note,Each region past the Bay gets its own ground, plants and landmarks: Morrowind's ash and giant mushrooms, Black Marsh's Hist, Summerset's vineyards. Off keeps each climate's original look.

features.tamrielMap.note,The enhanced map zooms out to all of Tamriel: its provinces, cities, mountains and seas, hand-drawn and joined to the Bay’s own coast. With Land beyond the Bay on, fast travel reaches them, except into or out of Cyrodiil online.
account.refusal.guildInvited,That guild already invited you. Answer its invitation instead.
features.torchesFromItems.effect,Takes effect at once; new characters and shop stock follow it.
features.torchesFromItems.note,Your light in dungeons comes from a torch, lantern or candle you carry, and it burns down, instead of a light you always have. Off by default in Daggerfall Unity.

features.townWatch.note,When a monster attacks you in a town and you’re not wanted, the town guard comes to help, then leaves once it’s safe. Commit a crime and they come for you as usual. Off keeps the classic guard, which only shows up for crimes.
features.unifiedBank.note,Access your deposited gold and bank accounts across all regional bank branches in Tamriel.
account.refusal.guildLogo,Your guild's logo is under review. Withdraw it on the Arms page, or wait for the moderators.

features.variedDungeonMonsters.note,Random monsters are picked from the dungeon’s full list around your level, so a dungeon has more variety instead of the same few. Off by default in Daggerfall Unity.
features.wagonUpkeep.effect,Takes effect at once. Online, each player picks their own.

features.wagonUpkeep.note,Your wagon wears as it rolls and on long journeys, and a Wagon Yard or a Wagon Repair Kit mends it. On Boons wear costs nothing; on Hard a worn wagon is slower and sells for less; Off is the classic wagon.
features.waterQuality.note,How detailed the enhanced water is. Full shows what lies under the surface and ripples where things move; Simple is lighter on your machine.
account.refusal.guildMarksFull,A guild's treasury holds at most {max, number} silver.

features.weaponGlow.note,A weapon with a fire, frost or shock damage bonus wears a moving outline of its element, brighter the stronger it is, and an enchanted Morrowind weapon glows. Off draws weapons as before.

features.weatherEvents.note,Rain, storms and snow move across the land with the wind, so you can see a storm coming, walk into it and out the other side. Off uses the classic weather, the same everywhere in the region.
features.wetWorld.note,After rain the ground darkens and puddles shine. Wet is sheen and ripples; Full also mirrors buildings in them. Off stays dry.
account.refusal.guildMarksShort,The treasury does not hold that much silver.
features.wildernessCamps.note,Out in the wilds you sometimes meet a small group of enemies, a camp or a roaming pack, instead of only one at a time. Off keeps the classic single encounters.
features.wildlife.note,Birds, bats and small animals live outdoors. Flocks cross the sky, birds sit on roofs and fly off as you come near, and small animals run from your feet.
features.wind.note,See the wind in the enhanced outdoors: trees and plants lean and sway with it, and faint streaks of air show which way it blows and how hard.

menu.online.modsNote,Most mods are your choice online. A few are set for everyone, so all players share the same ground and rules. Ground: Basic Roads, World of Daggerfall, Iliac Puddle No More’s sea and depth, and There’s a Hole in the Bottom of the Ocean. Rules: every setting of Meaner Monsters, the Combat and Armor Overhaul, Unleveled Loot, Roleplay & Realism, Roleplay & Realism: Items and Oblivion leveling, except who stands behind shop counters and which leveling your character uses. Travel Options is on for everyone, so every trip over land is traveled and ships sail only from ports. Immersive Travel is on for everyone too: carriages wait at every city gate, a driver’s fare is your fast travel over land, and fares are the same for everyone. Its map style stays your choice.
menu.online.needsAccount,Online needs an account, so no one else can use your name. Playing as a guest takes one click and no email.
menu.online.noSaves,Each offline character can be brought online from here, once.

menu.online.rules,Everyone plays their own save, and you can see and talk to each other anywhere. Dungeons and buildings are shared: enemies, doors, levers and opened chests are the same for everyone and stay that way. In towns and the wilds, everyone nearby sees the same monsters and can fight them, and they can hurt you too. {skyDay} The world’s clock and sky run on real time. Resting, travel, jail and training don’t move them, so a quest waiting for a time of day waits for the world’s, and a lycanthrope’s full moon lasts one night. Your character also has their own clock. It runs while you play and stops while you are logged off. Resting, travel, jail and training use it. Your wounds, spells, hunger, diseases, curses, guild ranks, rented rooms, loans and repairs run on it. Quest timers run on the world’s clock while you play. Resting, waiting and traveling don’t use up a quest’s days, and time logged off never counts. A quest that only asks you to wait, like a letter or “come back in a few days”, moves on after a couple of minutes of play. Rest at a fire, a tent or a bed: a night passes at once, at most once every 10 minutes of play, and party members within 15 meters sleep with you. Every enhancement is on for everyone, but your interface is your own. Most mods stay your choice online. A few are set for everyone: those that change the ground, monsters, loot or the rules. The Mods page marks each one.

Buy parts or a deed at a shipyard, put it in the water (a deed works only near a port) and take the helm to row, or raise the sails and trim them to the wind. Pack it up to take with you. It holds what you and your cart carry and shows on the travel map.

mods.foraging.Enabled.description,Gather in the wilderness: chop wood with a Wood-Axe, mine gems and metals with a Pick-Axe, cut plants with a Sickle, rob graves with a Spade, fish with a Fishing-Net and forage for food with a Basket. You gather by day, away from towns and enemies, and your attributes, the climate and the season decide what you find.

mods.horseCartAndCargo.Persistence.PhysicalPersistence.description,Your horse and wagon stay where you leave them. Off, they are always with you, as in the classic game.
mods.horseCartAndCargo.Presentation.ShowTrailingWagon.description,Shows the wagon trailing behind you when you ride with your cart. Off hides only that wagon.
mods.horseCartAndCargo.WagonAccess.InteriorAccessDistance.description,How close to a building or dungeon entrance your wagon must be for you to use it from inside.

mods.iliacPuddleNoMore.Enabled.description,A real sea: the seafloor drops away from every coast to as deep as 250 meters. Swim in open water with a breath meter among fish, weed, coral, shipwrecks, sunken loot and whatever lives in the deep.
mods.iliacPuddleNoMore.General.DecorationPopulateRadius.description,How far from you the seafloor is decorated, in map squares. At 3 nothing pops in
account.refusal.profMasterLines,Choose three different lines this piece can carry, with at most one effect.
mods.iliacPuddleNoMore.General.EnableSwimStroke.description,Press Run while swimming for a burst of speed
mods.iliacPuddleNoMore.General.MaxDecorationsPerTile.description,Maximum decorations per map square. Lower runs faster
account.refusal.profNeedAccount,The Stores are kept for registered accounts. Add a username to gather.
mods.immersiveFootsteps.ArmorSwaySettings.AllowArmorSwaySounds.description,Your armor makes a sound as you move
mods.immersiveFootsteps.ArmorSwaySettings.ArmorSwayFrequency.description,How often armor sounds play. Lower is more often
mods.immersiveFootsteps.Enabled.description,Footsteps that match the ground you walk on, and armour that rattles as you move.
mods.immersiveFootsteps.ErrorLoggingAndCompatibilitySettings.AllowModCompatWarnings.description,Warns you when another mod clashes with this one
mods.immersiveFootsteps.ErrorLoggingAndCompatibilitySettings.AllowVerboseErrorLogging.description,Has no effect here: this game keeps no error log.
mods.immersiveFootsteps.ErrorLoggingAndCompatibilitySettings.DoNotSpamExceptionsLogs.description,Has no effect here: this game keeps no error log.
mods.immersiveFootsteps.FootstepSettings.FootstepFrequency.description,How often footsteps sound. Lower is more often
account.refusal.profNoEssence,That piece carries too little enchantment to give any Arcane Essence.

mods.meanerMonsters.Enabled.description,Many monsters hit harder and take more to kill, while rats, bats and zombies are weaker. 20 monsters are changed, and werebeasts and the dragonling are bigger. With Physical Combat And Armor Overhaul also on, that mod’s version of these changes is used. With Daggerfall Enemy Expansion on, MUDEX, the author’s version made for it, is used instead.
mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.allowLuckIncrease.description,Allow Luck to be increased by more than one point

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.Enabled.description,Level up like Oblivion Remastered: every skill you raise fills a 100-point bar, and each level gives you virtues to spend on the attributes you choose. New characters are asked which system they want.
mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.luckIncreaseCost.description,Cost to upgrade Luck by one point
mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.majorSkillsImpact.description,Points given by a Major Skill level up (100 points required to level up)
mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.maxUpdatableAttribute.description,The number of attributes to be increased in one level up
account.refusal.profNoPackForm,That stays in the Stores and cannot go in your pack.
mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.minorSkillsImpact.description,Points given by a Minor Skill level up (100 points required to level up)
mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.miscSkillsImpact.description,Points given by a Misc Skill level up (100 points required to level up)

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.primarySkillsImpact.description,Points given by a Primary Skill level up (100 points required to level up). Morrowind has no Primary skills, so this starts equal to Major skills.

mods.oceanHoles.Enabled.description,Blue holes in the deep sea lead down to flooded dungeons with better loot. About 1 open-sea square in 48 has one: a black hole in the seafloor under a cloud of dark mist. Needs Iliac Puddle No More.
mods.oceanHoles.General.DungeonVisualDarkness.description,How dark the fog and light are in flooded dungeons
mods.oceanHoles.General.MiasmaHeight.description,Height of the mist over a hole
mods.oceanHoles.General.PitSpawnRate.description,How many blue holes there are: none at 0, 1 square in 48 at the middle, 1 in 24 at most
account.refusal.profNoPiece,Only a piece a crafter made online can be disenchanted.
mods.pcaao.armorHitFormulaRedone.description,Armor reduces the damage you take instead of making you harder to hit.
mods.pcaao.conditionBasedEffectiveness.description,Worn weapons and armor work less well. Needs Armor Hit Formula Redone.
mods.pcaao.criticalStrikesIncreaseDamage.description,Critical strikes raise your damage as well as your chance to hit. Needs Armor Hit Formula Redone.

mods.pcaao.Enabled.description,Armour reduces the damage you take instead of your chance to be hit, your skills decide whether you hit, shields block according to their material, and critical hits multiply damage. Off uses Daggerfall Unity’s combat.
mods.pcaao.equipmentDamageEnhanced.description,Your equipment wears out much faster, depending on its material, what hit it and more.
mods.pcaao.fadingEnchantedItems.description,Enchanted weapons and armor are destroyed when they break in combat. Needs Equipment Damage Enhanced.
mods.pcaao.fixedStrengthDamageModifier.description,Strength adds 1 damage per 10 points, as in the classic game, instead of 2.
account.refusal.profNotYours,That piece is not yours to disenchant.
mods.pcaao.softMaterialRequirements.description,Weapons below the material an enemy needs can still hurt it, at a large damage penalty. Needs Armor Hit Formula Redone.

mods.roadsHazelnut.Enabled.description,Hazelnut’s roads, tracks, rivers and streams across the whole Iliac Bay, painted onto the land. Off, the game builds its own roads between the towns on your map.
mods.roadsHazelnut.RiversAndStreams.description,Draws rivers and streams on the land.
mods.roadsHazelnut.SmoothRoads.description,Lightly smooths road surfaces. Turn it off for slightly better performance.
mods.roleplayRealism.advancedArchery.description,Alters to-hit and damage done by arrows depending on the length of draw.
mods.roleplayRealism.autoExtinguishLight.description,Automatically extinguish any light sources when you exit a dungeon
mods.roleplayRealism.bandaging.description,Allows bandages to be used for healing based on medical skill.
mods.roleplayRealism.bedSleeping.description,Allows sleep to be initiated by clicking on a bed.
mods.roleplayRealism.classicStrengthDamageBonus.description,Shows the strength damage bonus at half, as the classic game did.
account.refusal.profPieceBusy,That piece is listed on the market, on its way to you, or placed in a home, so it cannot be disenchanted now.

mods.roleplayRealism.Enabled.description,Realism changes: bows by draw weight, no climbing with a weapon out, fairer swing speed and hit chance, bank loans by level, ships only from ports, a heavy-load penalty, lights out when you leave a dungeon, purification that cures poison, reworked class enemies, harsher guild expulsions, and beds you can click to sleep in.
mods.roleplayRealism.encumbranceEffects.description,Provides speed and fatigue penalties when carrying too much weight.
mods.roleplayRealism.enemyAppearance.description,Remixes human enemy appearance based on class
mods.roleplayRealism.EnhancedRiding.enhancedRiding.description,Enable enhanced horse riding module, improving presentation and allowing galloping.
mods.roleplayRealism.EnhancedRiding.followTerrainSoftenFactor.description,How much the ride smooths out slopes, from 0 (none) to 32 (most).
mods.roleplayRealism.EnhancedRiding.GallopingInTowns.description,Enables galloping (sprinting) while riding horses in towns.
mods.roleplayRealism.EnhancedRiding.RealisticMovement.description,Makes the horse and cart movement backwards and sideways more realistic and limited.
mods.roleplayRealism.EnhancedRiding.TrampleCivilians.description,Enables the crime of trampling innocent townsfolk when galloping in a town. Be careful!
mods.roleplayRealism.equipDamage.description,Increases equipment damage proportional to max condition.
account.refusal.profPieceGone,That piece is not loose in your pack, so it cannot be disenchanted.
mods.roleplayRealism.loanAmountPerLevel.description,Sets the maximum amount per level that can be borrowed from banks
mods.roleplayRealism.purificationPotion.description,Changes purification potion to cure poison rather than grant invisibility
mods.roleplayRealism.RefinedTraining.intensiveTraining.description,Enables intensive training option for a session per day for five days, for extra cost.
mods.roleplayRealism.RefinedTraining.variableTrainingPrice.description,Makes price of training based on skill level as well as player level.
mods.roleplayRealism.shipPorts.description,Player can only board their ship when in a port town.
mods.roleplayRealism.underworldExpulsion.description,Enables underworld guilds to expel members for poor performance... with prejudice.
mods.roleplayRealism.variantNpcs.description,Enable variant NPC sprites in shops & taverns
mods.roleplayRealism.variantResidents.description,Fills 80% of houses with the townsfolk you see walking around, instead of random adventurers
mods.roleplayRealism.weaponMaterials.description,Moderates the to-hit bonuses of weapon materials so skill remains key factor
account.codes.copyRefused,The browser blocked copying to the clipboard. Save them as a file instead.
account.refusal.profPixel,The land here does not match the server's map. The game may need updating.
mods.roleplayRealism.weaponSpeed.description,Lowers weapon damage per second for characters with high Speed.
mods.roleplayRealismItems.alchemistPotions.description,Adds random potions for sale at alchemist stores, for a premium price
mods.roleplayRealismItems.bandaging.description,Allows bandages to stack, and to be used for healing based on medical skill
mods.roleplayRealismItems.conditionBasedPrices.description,Item prices are based on condition and loot you find can be quite worn out
mods.roleplayRealismItems.Enabled.description,Adds 2 new weapons and light and medium armor sets in every metal, and changes what items weigh and cost.
mods.roleplayRealismItems.lootRebalance.description,Rebalances loot on mobs and in piles
mods.roleplayRealismItems.newArmor.description,Adds new chest, arm, leg and foot armor pieces to the game
mods.roleplayRealismItems.newWeapons.description,Adds two new weapons to the game, Archers Axe and Light Flail
mods.roleplayRealismItems.realisticEnemyEquipment.description,Enemy equipment is realistic for their class and can be variable condition
mods.roleplayRealismItems.skillBasedStartingEquipment.description,Player starting equipment is based on skills
account.refusal.profRank,Your craft is not yet skilled enough for that.
mods.roleplayRealismItems.skillBasedStartingSpells.description,Player starting spells are based on skills
mods.roleplayRealismItems.storeQualityItemCondition.description,Items in shops can be in a used condition dependent on the quality of the store
mods.roleplayRealismItems.weaponBalance.description,Balances weapon attack speed and damage ranges against weight to give more valid choices
mods.seasonsIliacBay.Enabled.description,Trees, rocks and plants change with autumn, spring and winter. Add your own copy of the mod under Your own textures, or the classic look is used.
mods.shieldWidget.Animation.Direction.description,Set which animations will play during actions

mods.shieldWidget.Bob.Length.description,Amount of bobs in a single stride

mods.shieldWidget.Bob.SpeedMove.description,Speed of transition between stationary and moving
mods.shieldWidget.Compatibility.TextureScaleFactor.description,Divides the sprite’s pixel size. Raise it if a replacement texture pack draws the shield too large.

mods.shieldWidget.Enabled.description,See your shield in first person, which the original game never shows. It is drawn in its own metal, gets battered as it wears, and moves out of the way when you sheathe, swing or cast.
mods.shieldWidget.Inertia.ForwardDepth.description,Multiplier for the change in scale when moving forward or backward

account.refusal.profReforge,Arcane Essence can reforge a line on a Magic or Rare piece, but never on a Legendary, Aetheric or artifact piece.
mods.shieldWidget.Modules.Animation.description,Animation: the shield is raised and lowered frame by frame instead of sliding (art by WilhelmBlack).
mods.shieldWidget.Modules.Bob.description,Bob: the shield sways as you walk.
mods.shieldWidget.Modules.Inertia.description,Inertia: the shield trails behind as you look around and move.
mods.shieldWidget.Modules.Recoil.description,Recoil: a blow that lands on the shield rocks it and makes it ring. Needs Physical Combat and Armor Overhaul.
mods.shieldWidget.Modules.Step.description,Step: the shield’s position is rounded so it moves in steps.
account.refusal.profRespecPending,This craft's specialization was changed less than {days} days ago. The next change opens {days} days after the last.
account.refusal.profRid,That request could not be read. Try again.
mods.shieldWidget.Recoil.Condition.description,Event required for the shield to recoil

mods.shieldWidget.Recoil.Speed.description,The speed that the shield recovers from recoil

mods.shieldWidget.Shield.ConditionThresholdUpper.description,Condition, in percent, below which the shield first looks damaged.
mods.shieldWidget.Shield.LockAspectRatio.description,Enable to prevent the sprite from stretching or squishing depending on the screen's aspect ratio
account.refusal.profSculptor,Only a Sculptor can carve stone decor. Choose it at Masonry 100, under Building.
mods.shieldWidget.Shield.OffsetHorizontal.description,Offsets the sprite relative to the left edge of the screen
mods.shieldWidget.Shield.OffsetVertical.description,Offsets the sprite relative to the bottom edge of the screen
mods.shieldWidget.Shield.WhenAttacking.description,The shield's behavior when attacking with a weapon
mods.shieldWidget.Shield.WhenCasting.description,The shield's behavior when readying or while casting a spell
mods.shieldWidget.Shield.WhenSheathed.description,The shield's behavior when sheathing your weapon
